deepdive.sec: Wind Energy Casting & Green Industrial Components

bull_bear.body: Debt-funded capex (₹160-165Cr net debt); focus on utilization optimization before new capex; dividend policy not disclosed; reinvestment prioritized over buybacks or dividends
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility (steel, energy) with 1-2 quarter lag; geopolitical disruption in shipping routes (Middle East); ramp-up delays in new capacity; labor training and operational synchronization; legal dispute with MSCB over solar banking policy
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but confident in FY27 margin recovery; emphasizes operational discipline, pricing power, and long-term capacity needs; management is proactive on customer diversification and cost control
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 12 new product developments in FY26 (including for Vestas, L&T) significantly increase complexity but also revenue potential; machining utilization at 50% already despite only 30-40% product development complete — indicates faster-than-expected learning curve; INR depreciation vs Yuan (20%) is a bigger competitive advantage than vs USD (10%)
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet as at 30.06.26 (Rs Crore, unaudited): Net Worth 100.98, Long Term Borrowings 162.75, Short Term Borrowings 79.93, against Total Assets of 466.53 — borrowings exceed net worth on the deck's own figures.
- Non-Current Assets of 297.22 Rs Crore as at 30.06.26 (299.76 as at 31.03.26) reflect the capital already sunk into the 45,000 TPA build.
- The deck states no dividend, buyback or payout policy, and does not disclose how the proposed greenfield expansion to over 100,000 MT would be funded.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Wind domestic: Primary revenue driver; OEM exports: 25-30% of revenue; Direct exports: Stable; Gearbox: Growing segment; Non-wind: New customers added (Mahindra, L&T, Terex, Millikron, Willow)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "Working with 6 out of 15 Leading Wind OEMs", with customers shown split between wind and non-wind and a named customer described as "(erstwhile Siemens Gamesa)".
- SWOT strengths cited: "Ability to Produce large castings up to 30 MT", "Established products with Top Global OEMs" and "Ability to build large capacities with capital efficiency".
- Entry-barrier framing: "Excellent growth opportunities in Renewable's with high entry barriers", plus "India is being converted as manufacturing Hub offers growing casting demand", "Trade wars/Global Sentiments favor India's demand" and "INR depreciation against USD and CNY, favouring Indian foundries".
- Acknowledged constraints: "Limited Capacity compared to peers (scaled up to 45,000 TPA, planning to expand further)" and "Dependency on outsourced machining (~20,000 TPA in-house machining established)".
- Part of the Shirgaokar Brothers Group (Since 1913), whose businesses are listed as Sugar, Foundry, General Engineering, IT & Hospitality with a group annual turnover of Rs 2,700 Crores — a group figure, not the listed entity's.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Guidance] "FY 27 is expected to have a ~33% revenue growth over FY 26", with the revenue-streams chart showing FY 26-27 P of 500 Rs Cr versus 376 Rs Cr in FY 25-26, "Based on executable Order Book Projection" — management flags this projection "may be subject to change based on market conditions".
- [Guidance] "Despite moderation in Q1, FY27 PBDIT margin is expected to improve by >300 bps, driven by higher volumes, increased export contribution and growing contributions from in-house machining."
- [Industry - wind] "India's installed wind capacity to more than double from 51 GW in 2026 to 107 GW by 2030" and "Global cumulative capacity projected to exceed 2 TW by 2030, driven by record-breaking annual installations" (source: GEWC Global Wind Report 2026).
- [Industry - castings] 2024 casting market of 110 Mn MT total, "Global: $ 160 bn" and "India: $ 13.2 bn"; large casting demand split "Wind : 1.5 Mn MT" and "Non-Wind: ~6 Mn MT" (sources: Indian Institute of Foundrymen, Foundry Planet).
- [Exceptional item] The income statement records exceptional items described as "statutory provision for new labour code" — 0.01 Rs Crore for the quarter ended 31.03.26 and 0.65 Rs Crore for the year ended 31.03.26.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margin compression due to: (1) higher outsourcing during transition, (2) new facility overheads, (3) discounted export pricing (in-house machining not yet operational), (4) commodity/energy inflation from West Asia; FY27 margin recovery expected via utilization leverage, price pass-throughs, and INR depreciation benefit
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 33% to ₹500Cr; margin: +300+ bps to ~16.1%; order inflow: Strong, with new customers (Mahindra, L&T) and Vestas contract pending; capex/commissioning: No new capex announced, land acquisition targeted for FY27 to support next expansion
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: ₹500-530Cr visibility, with confirmed orders from Vestas, Siemens Gamesa (Viona), Nordex, GE, Envision, Adani, Flender, ZF, Mahindra, L&T
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Next capacity expansion (beyond 45K MT) contingent on land acquisition in FY27; potential to reach ₹780Cr+ revenue with full product mix utilization; solar captive power (10MW) reduces energy cost volatility
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Synergy Green expanded foundry and machining capacity to 45K and 20K MT/year, enabling 5MW turbine production and driving 33% FY27 revenue guidance to ₹500Cr, but FY26 margins were pressured by transition costs and commodity inflation; margin expansion of 300+ bps is expected in FY27 as utilization ramps and pricing pass-throughs catch up.
